guidance.opening:
一九二〇年秋天，波士顿。你坐在一位房东的办公室里；他让人把你找来，因为有一栋房子空着，没人肯再租。桌面上有一股淡淡的烟草味。

房东霍华德·克兰靠着椅背，语气像街边闲聊：「上一户科斯塔家走得匆忙，人进了病院。街坊把那地方说得邪乎，我只想弄清楚里头到底怎么了，好让房子还能租得出去。你来一趟，我先听听你是谁。」

他朝你点了点下巴，问：「你叫什么，平时靠什么吃饭？随便说说就行。」
guidance.advice: Use only listed occupation names. Public premise: visitor summoned to a Boston landlord's office in autumn 1920 over a house that will not re-let after the last tenants left for an asylum; do not treat hire, keys, cash, address, or a written report as already settled. Professions that fit the public story without forcing a choice: Journalist, Private Investigator, Lawyer, Police Detective, Police Officer, Librarian, Professor, Author, Antiquarian, Doctor of Medicine, Parapsychologist, Clergy, Engineer, Dilettante. Useful training/languages (optional, no numbers): English literacy and Library Use or Law for paper trails; Credit Rating for talking to landlords and clerks; Occult only as rumor-level curiosity, not proof. Era belongings: notebook, fountain pen, street clothes, streetcar fare—not house keys or an advance. Optional ties (not facts): knew a former tenant socially; answered a notice; referred by someone who deals in property. Optional motivation questions in conversation, not a form: why they came when asked; whether they work days or nights. Preserve uncertainty: neighbors' talk is talk. Crane's magician hobby and chase alley are not part of identity setup.
guidance.handoff: The visitor is in Howard Crane's Boston office, autumn 1920, having been sent for about a house that will not re-let after the last tenants (the Costas) left for an asylum. Crane has asked who they are and what they do; identity is not decided and no commission, keys, cash, or address have been taken. Continue from this meeting in the office once the investigator card exists.
